# YM23: 濂溪乐处 Lianxi Lechu, "The Happy Place of Falling Streams"

Malone calls it Lien Hsi Lo Ch'u.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM23` · Page: `/scenes/#YM23` · Row: `research/buildings/YM23-lianxi-lechu/`

## What it was

濂溪乐处 Lianxi Lechu, an island hall north-west of 水木明瑟, ringed by pond and stream: the nine-bay main hall (eave plaque 慎修思永 Shenxiu Siyong), 云香清胜 behind, 芰荷深处 on the east wall, the gallery 香雪廊 turning north-east, the tower 云霞舒卷 and a pavilion 临泉 (S05 j82:1a-b; E1703). To the south the flower-god temple 汇万总春之庙 with the five-bay 蕃育群芳, 香远益清楼, 乐天和, 味真书屋, 池水共心月同明 and 普济桥 (S05 j82:2a-b; E1704, E2376). S361 adds 水云居, 荷香书屋, 延云殿, a seven-bay 知过堂 and 墨光亭 (E1709). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 慎修思永 and 知过堂 (YM23-01, YM23-N01) stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).

From the inventory row: **built** 雍正 (慎修思永 S43); **changed** Water porch and rocky pavilion removed before the official map (S02 p.91); differs on plans (S41); **destroyed** 1860; 慎修思永 and 知过堂 on the 1873 survival list (S06) (S05, S02, S08, S41, S43, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "苑中菡萏甚多此處特盛小殿數楹流水周環於其下" (S05 j82:1b-2a): the garden has many lotuses but here most; a small hall of a few bays with water flowing round under it; the poem names Zhou Dunyi, the lover of lotus.

### How later sources differ

Malone notes that the plan S01 lacks the long covered porch on piles round the lotus pond and the open pavilion south of the island that the leaf shows, probably removed by then (E1708, S02); S01 adds 知过堂 (YM23-N01, seven bays) and 水云居 (YM23-N03), names not in S05. So the 1860 state differs from the leaf: drop the pile gallery.
